content.title: About
content.content: Beans and rice with tomatoes is a classic dish that combines protein‑rich beans, carbohydrate‑dense rice, and flavorful tomatoes. It is popular in many cuisines where simple, hearty, and nutritious meals are valued.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are an excellent source of plant protein and fiber.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their bright red color.
The bean‑rice combination provides a complete set of essential amino acids.
The dish can be easily adapted with different spices, vegetables, or meats.
Tomatoes help improve iron absorption from beans.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beans supply plant protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and potassium in beans and rice help regulate cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene and vitamin C from tomatoes protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Steady energy release
items.content: Complex carbohydrates in rice release glucose slowly, providing lasting satiety.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from beans and tomatoes promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; soaking beans before cooking helps.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the dish is prepared with added salt or sauces, monitor overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or as a side. It stores well in the refrigerator and can be reheated. Enhance flavor with fresh herbs, spices, a drizzle of olive oil, or a sprinkle of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consuming.
